quest.title: The Mysterious Wangsheng Parlor
quest.description: Your adventure takes you to Wuwang Hill, where Paimon senses that something is amiss...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—Why did we come here? Paimon's got a bad feeling about this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not that Paimon's scared or anything, just... concerned for your safety.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's just that this is how lots of scary stories go — you're in an empty place in the middle of nowhere, there's barely any light, and then just when you least expect it, a stranger comes out of—

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: —Ah?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Waaaaaah! Quick {NICKNAME}, do something!!!

choices.text: Didn't you say you weren't scared?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's intuition says that anyone we run into here is going to be far from normal!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If he gets us, he's gonna eat Paimon for sure!

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Wh—Who are you?

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: T—Traveler? Are you from one of the other nations? No, I've never seen your kind of attire before...

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Could it be that you t—traveled from... the other side!?

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: I'm just here for a funeral — I don't mean to offend. No matter who you are, there's no need for any ill will between us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew, seems he's just your average scaredy-cat. He looks more afraid than Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep yep! You should leave the introductions to Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't be afraid, we come in peace.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: —Aaaah! Gods protect me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, no! Stop freaking out, and stand still! Relax!

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: "Relax"!? Yes, whatever you say! Please, stay your hand!

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Don't come any closer! I mean you no harm! Don't! Don't touch me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Paimon already said, nothing's gonna happen!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Am not! Paimon's super friendly-looking.

choices.text: I came from beyond the heavens.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: "Beyond the heavens"? A strange way of putting it...

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: D—Don't try to scare me!

choices.text: Didn't you say you were concerned about my safety?

talks.objective: Catch up to the fleeing Meng

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Director! Director! There's a ghost after me!
Oh?
Ha, don't get too excited. These are clients, not ghosts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! We said we're not ghosts. Why won't you calm down and let us explain?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although... "clients" doesn't seem quite right either.
Aiya, forgive me, this is one of our new undertakers, Meng. It's his first time working a funeral, so of course, he's afraid of his own shadow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Funeral... Funeral... Oh! The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor — Zhongli is a consultant there. They deal with this stuff a lot, right?
Oh, you know Zhongli? Well! That saves me a lot of explaining.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I'm Hu Tao, the current director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, responsible for... well, trifling matters having to do with mortality.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: A satisfying trade to be in, though, and Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is well-known around town. Whatever the request, I'd be glad to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't think we fall into the "client" category.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, if we were looking for Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's help, this is hardly the place we would come to.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ah but you see, I wasn't referring to clients in the business sense. Everyone who enters this mortal realm will be a client of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Sooner or later...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well that's dark!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor welcomes advance reservations! When you choose us, you'll never have to worry about what might be around the corner.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: But be sure to book the right date! Pro tip: it is a living nightmare trying to get flowers at short notice...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Speaking of dates, if you're struggling to decide, please do come and talk it over. I'd hate to see you still alive and kicking when your big day comes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Slow down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's— You— ... There's a lot to unpack here...

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: You'll have to excuse her. The director is a rather unique individual. Allow me to explain.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: We heard that there'd been some supernatural activity at Wuwang Hill. To restore calm here, we performed a funeral ceremony.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: It went very smoothly! According to the director, we shouldn't be expecting any more issues in the near future.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, Wuwang Hill, funeral... What more is there to say? These three belong in the same sentence.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: You two on the other hand, have no business coming to Wuwang Hill. You being here is not normal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm... Maybe your understanding of "normal" isn't quite normal?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm here on an adventure.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Adventure? Aha, you must hail from the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Then you are one of our distinguished clients! "Wood," to be precise.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Wood"? What do you mean?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: That's just how we gauge our client's importance. We have four levels: "wicker," "bamboo," "wood," and "marble." The higher the grade, the better we'd like to get to know you.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: But I've just only heard of this!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Well, that's because I only just thought of it. Oh, don't look so shocked.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Take a look, our adventurers spend the whole day scaling mountains, clearing domains, and smiting enemies. Danger and peril are their bread and butter.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Clients like these deserve better treatment. Taking an interest in their daily lives will ultimately benefit not only them, but also me...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Eh, touched a nerve, did I? I'd have thought any adventurers who dare come here would be used to conversations like this.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Anyway, I have a favor to ask. Recently, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor has been trying to strike a business deal with the Adventurers' Guild. With you acting as an intermediary, it would be so much easier.

choices.text: I don't really want to take part in your business.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hmm, let me think what I could offer you as a reward. Or perhaps there's a favor I could do in return?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, we're looking for someone! We've asked a lot of people, but nobody seems to have a clue where they are.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: This seems like something right up my alley. I can even inquire with "the ones who no longer speak" for you.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: You see! Helping me will be worth your while... Come on then, my able assistants! Let's get down to Liyue Harbor and do some business!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, when did we become your assistants!?

choices.text: Is everyone at Wangsheng Funeral Parlor a weirdo?

talks.objective: Accompany Hu Tao to the Adventurers' Guild

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Ugh, you again... Look, I told you, we're not interested in the kind of cooperation you describe.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Come on, there's no reason to get upset. Look, one of your members is an avid supporter of my proposition!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Since our last negotiation, I've come up with a new proposal, which I think you'll find has far more benefits for you.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: First things first, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor will prioritize the Adventurers' Guild requests above all others. You'll also receive 100 of our signature wooden coffins for free, together with your first order.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: That's not all! We also provide an on-site cadaver collection service covering almost all regions in Liyue. Now, we do charge a slight premium for a very small number of especially dangerous areas, but... but don't you worry about that, I promise you it's still very affordable!

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I don't think you're hearing me...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Okay, alright. I get it, you want to bargain a little more. But our offer as it stands is already quite a good deal, don't you think?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Just think about it. An adventurer's life is full of unexpected threats. It's only natural to take precautions. "Mend the roof before it rains," as they say.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Yeah... no. I'm not so sure that saying applies in this context.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Speaking of precautions, I'd rather focus on keeping my adventurers safe in the first place.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: It's time for you to go. I have to attend to other matters.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Wait, hold on! Wh—What would you say to a group discount!? Thirty percent off for parties of ten!

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Director! Please, you did your best... We don't need another clash with the Millelith.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... If Paimon understood all that correctly, it seems like she's trying to sell them the funeral parlor's services.

choices.text: I side with Lan on this issue.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Aiya, nothing left to do here. Let's go back to Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

talks.objective: Go back to the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor with Hu Tao

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: *sigh* Seems like the old ways are the most reliable after all.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Meng, are you done preparing our promotional materials?

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Ah... My apologies, I'm only about halfway through. Do you really think they'll be effective?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Trust me, they're going to work wonders. This marketing strategy has been used by Wangsheng Funeral Parlor for generations.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Clients in need come to our door and write down their commissions on blank wooden tiles. Then, they squeeze those inside the parlor through the crack under the door.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I fulfill the request written on each tile to make sure our clients are satisfied with the service, no matter if it's an obituary, cremation, or funeral that they seek.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Although... it is a bit of a hassle with the constant back and forth. If only we could burn 'em by the batch...

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: No, director, I'm not asking about the wooden tiles themselves but about the "special offer" they advertise.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hehe, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor should keep up with the times! Just think about it! If we don't attract new clients, we'll be left with nothing, won't we?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Business development is a crucial element of every prosperous enterprise. I've been trying various marketing strategies ever since I became the director.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I put up posters, just like all the other shops, but the Millelith promptly removed them.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Then, I organized the "Wangsheng Visitor's Day," but no one showed up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well that doesn't come as a huge surprise...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: And finally, I discovered that the traditional ways are the most reliable after all. I took inspiration from the wisdom of previous directors.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: So now, I go from door to door, looking for people and organizations willing to cooperate. Just like during our visit to the Adventurers' Guild! That's what I mean by "business development."

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: The other method I'm trying is using the wooden tiles as coupons. Just by writing things like "Buy one, get one free for the holder of this tile" on them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What do they buy and what do they get?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hehe, a solid and durable "second home," of course.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: They may not need it right away, but they can be sure that when they do, it will still be as good as new. "It won't start deteriorating before you finish doing so yourself" — that's the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor quality guarantee.

choices.text: ...I don't know what to say to that.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Alright Meng, keep adding those special offers to the wooden tiles! The future of our business depends on it.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: I'm still not sure this will work...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oh, I get it! You think that our special offer is not comprehensive enough, right?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: It is true, I was offering all kinds of great benefits to the Adventurers' Guild because they are a new client.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: But in doing so, I neglected my old clients. You're right, it's unfair.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hmm, let me do some market research! Wait here, my faithful assistants, I'll be back with you in a moment. It shouldn't take too long.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon already told you, we're not your assistants!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Guess we got dragged into somebody else's business AGAIN. Let's look around while she's away.

choices.text: No wonder you're on the Millelith's radar.
Didn't you say the wooden tiles should be blank?

talks.objective: Investigate the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's surroundings while waiting for Hu Tao

dialogues.speaker: Examine Board
dialogues.text: (A board used for hanging Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's wooden tiles. According to Hu Tao, all the tiles should be blank...)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Board
dialogues.text: (...In which case, the characters on the back of the tiles must be the "special offer.")

talks.objective: Investigate the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's surroundings while waiting for Hu Tao

dialogues.speaker: Examine Door
dialogues.text: (So, behind this door is Wangsheng Funeral Parlor...)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Door
dialogues.text: (It looks far more ordinary than the director made it out to be.)

talks.objective: Investigate the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's surroundings while waiting for Hu Tao

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: You must be the Director's new hires?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not us! We're just very curious about Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and Hu Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Well, I wouldn't get too curious if I were you. Too much knowledge isn't good for ordinary folk.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: The director is tactful when it comes to what should and shouldn't be known.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Her? Tactful?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That's settled then, write it like this:

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: "Wangsheng Funeral Parlor Bumper Sale! Buy One, Get One Free! Buy Two, Get Three Free! More For Your Mora!"

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hee-hee! I love it, better than all that lifeless brochure stuff. We want people to feel warm and fuzzy.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: But Director... Isn't lifeless the name of the game in this industry?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That's old hat, we're opening up new ground.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Why does Wangsheng Funeral Parlor need to open up... *sigh* Yes, Director.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Poor guy's given up...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Right, we should get going. I am not letting new business escape us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "We"? ...As in, us?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Who else? Do you see anyone else around here? ...Well, you probably wouldn't see them if there was.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Stop adding little afterthoughts like that! Creeps people out!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, just a joke, sorry. Everything you see is everything that's present. For the moment, at least.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Ah, lighten up! The way I see it, people make death scarier than it really is.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: What people truly fear about departing this world is suffering and regret. To deal with the trauma, they let their imaginations run wild with notions of ghosts and evil spirits.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: All baseless fantasies. What we've ended up with is a topic that people are morbidly afraid of talking about... If I don't broach the subject, then Wangsheng Funeral Parlor won't be long for this world.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But... I've seen a ghost.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oh? More approachable and appeasable than you'd imagined?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, Paimon wouldn't say that. Let's just say, at least it didn't hurt us...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: You must have come across a particularly ferocious entity. How should I put this... Most spirits are incapable of harming ordinary folks.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: The job of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is to "guard the border between life and death." One component of this is correcting notions of death and the afterlife that people may hold. Simply put, for those unable to see the "border," they're best kept as far away from it as possible.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: So for ordinary folks, the best-case scenario is ignorance of all matters concerning spirits and the afterlife — or even better, a belief that none of it exists.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then you really don't have any excuse for spooking the heck out of people!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Haha, you make it sound so abominable. I'm just trying to get them to see the humor in it all.

choices.text: That's why people think you're weird.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I never thought you'd be such a bore. Never mind! If you stick by me, everything will become clear.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Alright, let's get going. Follow me.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Director, wait — what about Big G? Don't forget...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Big G? Who's that? We've been in Liyue for ages and never heard that name.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oh nothing, just something Meng's been pleading with me to take care of. Should be a piece of cake.

choices.text: I've yet to see the funny side...
It's good to think before you speak.

talks.objective: Visit a potential client with Hu Tao

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu
dialogues.text: Uh... Sorry, who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hello! I'm Hu Tao, Director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu
dialogues.text: Okay, so why would someone from Wangsheng Funeral Parlor be looking for me?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Mmm... nothing major. How are you feeling these days? Any aches or pains?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You shouldn't ignore them, by the way. Very often, they're an omen of something terminal.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: When we're healthy, it's easy to forget the crushing fragility of life. So... aches and pains. Best to keep an eye on them.

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu
dialogues.text: What are you getting at!? I'm in great health and enjoying life very much, thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu
dialogues.text: Go and find some other poor soul! Goodbye!

dialogues.speaker: Mumu
dialogues.text: Uh, and you are? Be quick, I'm busy.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hello there, would you be interested in understanding a bit about our services at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor?

dialogues.speaker: Mumu
dialogues.text: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor? Uhhhh... I'm not in need of your services.

dialogues.speaker: Mumu
dialogues.text: So you're out here... looking for new customers? Don't you think this might be a bit of a crass way of going about it?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hardly. Isn't this the fashion these days? "Bring the service to the customer," and all that?

dialogues.speaker: Mumu
dialogues.text: I'm not sure it's every service that falls into that...

dialogues.speaker: Mumu
dialogues.text: Anyway, please bother someone else if you don't mind.

dialogues.speaker: Congzi
dialogues.text: I know your face... The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor Director, right? Sorry, I'm really in no need of—

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Don't apologize, get to know us! We've got a new sale going on.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ever hear the saying "out with the old, in with the new"? Well, going out with a bang is the best way to start off in style on the other side! Hee-hee.

dialogues.speaker: Congzi
dialogues.text: If you keep talking like this, I'll have to call the Millelith.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: No no no — okay, relax, we're leaving.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: But Wangsheng Funeral Parlor awaits your distinguished patronage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You really don't give up, do you?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hmm? Are you trying to make me feel better?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: ...Thank you. Seems you understand me far better than most people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not really, this is just getting really uncomfortable...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Enough "business development." Please, help me find someone.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: "Business development"? Is that what you see this as?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Surely you don't think all that was "business development"!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then what was it exactly!? Traumatization for its own sake!?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: No no no, the "business development" ended after the discussion with the Adventurers' Guild!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I was helping to find somebody for Meng. You remember Big G?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: As it turns out, the "Big G" that Meng is looking for is a ghost adrift in the mortal realm.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: The three we saw just now were all people I suspected of being followed by Big G. But having seen them, I didn't sense the presence of anything otherworldly.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: So we just had a quick chat, and I left it at that.

choices.text: If that was "stopping for a quick chat"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why didn't you say so? Paimon thought you had some kinda sixth sense for, uh... People in declining health...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Huh? What would I need that kind of ability for? I'm no doctor.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Haha! Were you seriously hoping that the Director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor was going to start healing people? Or...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon was trying to subtly imply that... Uh... never mind, Paimon wouldn't know how to explain subtlety in a way you'd understand...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Uh... Well, let's leave that for now and head back to Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. This Big G matter is very closely linked to Meng.

choices.text: I wonder what "business development" looks like...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I have a reputation for being a weirdo amongst the ranks of the Adventurers' Guild...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: But it's only because they haven't had an opportunity to talk to Hu Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hmm... The way we're wording this lacks... warmth and sincerity.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: If we're content to settle for just seeing people off, how can we give them a sense of really having "gained" something?

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: But... that's a tough feeling to convey in this industry...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Precisely the problem! If we can't get that feeling across, then how will we get return clients?

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: R—Return clients?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Just look for the director.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Stick close to the director, she knows what she's doing.

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu
dialogues.text: Don't bother me again! I'm doing just fine!

dialogues.speaker: Mumu
dialogues.text: Please, bother someone else if you don't mind.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: *sigh* Big G... How did it all turn out like this...

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Ah, don't mind me, just thinking out loud.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was it... something Paimon said?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go after him, he might do something stupid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, "the ones who no longer speak"... Did she mean talking to the dead?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... She's a weird one.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hmph, rejecting a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. It's their loss.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Some things are inevitable. It's only a matter of time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where are we going?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: To visit an important potential client. I'll lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ugh, why do they get angry? What's wrong with a few earnest health tips?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks it's because they're coming from the director of a funeral parlor...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ugh... another failure. Still, not the end of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's curious, does this approach ever work out for you?
